subject: [Mentors for Project] - Bayesian Network to system biology

messages.author: fe857a7d1d154963
messages.subject: [Mentors for Project] - Bayesian Network to system biology
parts:
Hello

I am Vinícius, currently graduated student in the Bioinformatics program at UFPR. My research uses the Bayesian Networks learning and inference to systems biology stuides. Initially, I used the bnlearn package to develop my study. I used the score-based Hill-Climbing to better understand the dependence among data elements. Although, the package algorithm has high computational and time expensive. So, I want to develop an improved functions to system biology by using the Bayesian networks learning, the Bayesian information Criterion and the Hill-Climbing scored-based.

For this project, I am looking for two mentors. One expert in R and another in Bayesian network learning and inference. Because I was working with these ideas and I had good results. I will be motivate to develop a more efficient tools focusing in the systems biology questions.I have an one year experience in R and statistics  in my masters degree. Also, I have developed my skills in octave and machine learning.Even if no one is interested to be my mentor, I'll appreciate any suggestion of materials and bibliography to develop my studies.

Thanks,
Vinícius Chagas

If you need help with R, I can be a co mentor. I have worked with GSoC R for last 4 years and have contributed to few packages on CRAN. Maintainer of one package and ready to submit second. I do work in broad biology domain but have no clue about Bayesian methods. So do let me know if you want me to be one co mentor.

Regards,

Vijay

messages.author: b98e21751c27e8b9
messages.subject: Re: [Mentors for Project] - Bayesian Network to system biology
parts:
If this is Bioinformatics, shouldn't the first outlet for this be
Bioconductor?

Also, it feels kind of late for students to be proposing new ideas with
no mentors. We announced our intent to participate again in GSoC months
ago, and asked for project ideas at that time and many times in
between.

I'm somewhat reluctant to take bets on unknown students with no mentors
identified. Vijay's offer is a kind one, as he has a track record of
success with GSoC as both a student and a mentor, but we'd really need
authors of related packages engaged in this, which I'm not seeing.

Regards,

Brian
